STEP 2 - ARCHIVE. The 'Archive' table's data rows must end up being EXACTLY these 8 rows, in exactly this order, top to bottom. Keep the table's header row and all of its formatting. Cells shown in quotes are literal - copy them exactly. Cells shown in angle brackets are for you to write. The rows, top to bottom, must be exactly: 'Week 11', 'Week 10', 'Week 9', 'Week 8', 'Week 7', 'Week 6', 'Week 5', 'Weeks 1-4 (rolled up)'. The first cell of each of those rows must read exactly as quoted, INCLUDING the word 'Week' - write 'Week 3', never '3'. The column is headed 'Week'; that heading is not a substitute for the label. Row 'Week 11' is NEW. Its Dates cell is '2026-03-16 to 2026-03-22'. Its Shipped cell is your own summary, at most 20 words, of EXACTLY this text and nothing else in the document: "Combat prototype merged to main behind a feature flag; Enemy AI flocking behaviour landed for Scrapper swarms; First playtest with eight external players (avg session 41 min); Audio middleware spike finished; Wwise selected over FMOD". Its Risks carried cell is your own summary, at most 15 words, of exactly these risks: "Crash rate above the cert threshold; Publisher marketing beats not aligned with content lock; Streaming budget overrun on the Drift Belt". Summarise the quoted text only - other steps in this instruction change the document, and this row must describe Week 11, not the week replacing it. Every other row keeps its existing cell contents exactly as they are - do not rewrite, reword or re-summarise them. STEP 3 - 'What changed'. Replace the ENTIRE
    element in that section with exactly this HTML, character for character:
    • Audio middleware spike finished; Wwise selected over FMOD
    • Grapple cooldown retuned from 8s to 5s after playtest data
    • Cinematic camera rig handed to the animation team
    • Localisation pipeline stubbed for 6 languages

      • Get the slice in front of the publisher
      • Second external playtest, 20 players
      REPLACEMENT MEANS REPLACEMENT: where this instruction lists what a section must contain, the section must end up containing exactly that and nothing else. Delete what is not on the list rather than keeping it alongside. Preserve all existing formatting exactly: the document title, every section heading, table borders, header-row shading, alternating row colours, fonts, font sizes and colours. Do not restyle anything. Do not add, remove or rename any heading. Do not reorder the sections. Copy every quoted or listed value character for character. Do not add a full stop to a bullet that has none, and do not reword anything. STRUCTURAL RULE: both tables must remain elements with their header rows intact. Never replace a table with a single row, a div or a list. Never drop a table's header row.
request.document_html:
Nebula Drift - Weekly Production Digest

Week 11 · 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-22 · Phase: Vertical Slice
Vantage Nine Studios · internal · standing document, edited in place every Monday

What changed

  • Combat prototype merged to main behind a feature flag
  • Enemy AI flocking behaviour landed for Scrapper swarms
  • First playtest with eight external players (avg session 41 min)
  • Audio middleware spike finished; Wwise selected over FMOD

What is at risk

RiskOwnerArea SeverityTrend
Crash rate above the cert thresholdDev H.QAMediumsteady
Publisher marketing beats not aligned with content lockMarcus O.ProductionMediumworsening
Streaming budget overrun on the Drift BeltYuki T.EngineeringHighsteady

What is next

  • Instrument the traversal funnel
  • Close the audio licence
  • Get the slice in front of the publisher

Archive

Newest first. Detail rows older than 8 weeks are folded into a single rolled-up row so this section stays readable at 52 weeks.

Week Dates Shipped Risks carried
Week 10 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-15 Cinematic camera rig handed off, localisation pipeline stubbed for 6 languages, and the vertical slice was playable. Crash threshold, marketing beats, and streaming budget remain risky.
Week 9 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-08 First playtest with eight external players; audio middleware chose Wwise over FMOD; grapple cooldown retuned. Crash threshold, subtitle sign-off, marketing alignment, and streaming budget remain risky.
Week 8 2026-02-23 to 2026-03-01 Vertical slice greyboxed and playable; combat prototype merged behind a feature flag Crash rate above cert threshold; subtitle sizing lacks accessibility sign-off
Week 7 2026-02-16 to 2026-02-22 Grapple cooldown retuned, camera rig handed off, localisation stubbed for six languages, slice playable start to finish Controller boss tuning, save-game versioning, matchmaking above 5k CCU, second designer delay
Week 6 2026-02-09 to 2026-02-15 Engine 5.4 merged; build times down 31%; art style narrowed to two directions; Drift Belt nav-mesh; Salvage spreadsheet first pass. Boss difficulty untuned for controller; save-game format still unversioned.
Week 5 2026-02-02 to 2026-02-08 Audio depot migrated to Git LFS; Grapple traversal prototype playable end to end on test level Boss encounter difficulty untuned for controller; outsourced character art slipping two weeks.
Weeks 1-4 (rolled up) 2026-01-05 to 2026-02-01 Art direction narrowed, engine upgrade merged, build times improved, and nav-mesh work progressed. Versioning, controller boss tuning, and art delivery remain risky.
